digest.intro: Triangles make a comeback, AI proves cryptography, and the world negotiates.

items.title: US-Iran: Military Campaign 'Quite Unlikely,' Qatari Talks 'Positive'
items.blurb: Trump said publicly a renewed strike on Iran 'doesn't seem to be necessary,' while Qatar's PM described talks with Trump and Vance as 'positive' — and will make an unscheduled stop at the G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris. Meanwhile France accused Iran's IRGC of a refrigeration-infrastructure cyberattack it called 'unprecedented in both scale and aggression,' which suggests the conflict is migrating into civilian infrastructure even as the kinetic phase cools.

items.title: Task Force Iron Gate: The Iran Blockade Moves Inland
items.blurb: CENTCOM quietly stood up Task Force Iron Gate on November 7th — only ~20 people, but the mandate is a structural shift: from maritime blockade to disrupting Iran's land-based supply networks for advanced weapons and dual-use technology. Small units with broad inter-agency coordination authority tend to punch far above their headcount; this is the quiet architecture of a long-duration pressure campaign, not an escalation toward strikes.

items.title: AlphaProof Code: AI Formally Verifies Signal's Cryptography at the Binary Level
items.blurb: DeepMind's AlphaProof Code wrote 6.5 million lines of Lean proof to mathematically verify that Signal's cryptographic protocol is correct — not at the spec level, but at the actual compiled AArch64 binary that runs on your phone. This is the first time any method, AI or human, has formally verified a widely deployed protocol's real implementation; artifacts are open-sourced. The implications for security-critical infrastructure are hard to overstate: 'it works in testing' just got a much more serious competitor.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2: Jagged AGI and Where the Gaps Still Are
items.blurb: Mollick got pre-release access to Fable 5.2 — the same model Anthropic says designed three working electronic devices from scratch, made progress on black-hole physics problems, and formalized Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours. His honest read: 'Jagged AGI' — genuinely capable of most expert intellectual tasks you can do at a computer, but with remaining gaps that are harder to characterize than simple hallucinations, which makes them more dangerous to miss. Worth reading before the hype layer fully solidifies.

items.title: Claude Code Is Silently Committing Your Secrets to GitHub
items.blurb: When you click 'Yes, and don't ask again' in Claude Code, your approval gets written to `.claude/settings.local.json` — sometimes including the full shell command you approved, passwords, API keys, and all. Anthropic adds this file to your global `.gitignore`, but not the repo-level one, so it leaks whenever a folder becomes a repo later or Claude Code commits changes on its own. Apiiro found over 100,000 exposed instances on GitHub. If you use Claude Code, check your repos now.

items.title: Blender 5.3: Native Gaussian Splat Support Arrives
items.blurb: Blender 5.3 ships native Gaussian Splat import and editing, NVIDIA DLSS denoising in the viewport (eliminating the flicker that made lighting dev painful), and panoramic camera support in EEVEE covering equirectangular, cubemap, fisheye, and mirror ball projections. The compositor also gets stackable Effects — Bloom, Chromatic Aberration, Film Grain, Vignette — applied like modifiers, plus 17 Geometry Nodes now usable directly in the compositor. For anyone moving between photogrammetry captures and real-time WebGL pipelines, the Splat integration alone is a genuine workflow unlock.

items.title: Triangle Splatting: Triangles Are Back as the Better Splat Primitive
items.blurb: A research group argues — convincingly — that the softness of Gaussian primitives is causing the blurring and loss of fine detail that everyone working with 3DGS has noticed, particularly at edges and occlusion boundaries. Triangle Splatting replaces Gaussians with differentiably rendered triangles, achieving 2,400+ FPS at 1280×720 on the Garden scene using a standard mesh renderer, while outperforming Zip-NeRF on indoor scenes for perceptual quality. Because triangles are native to the graphics stack, the path from capture to WebGL is suddenly a lot shorter.

items.title: DIAL: The 3D Printing Method That Finally Combines Speed, Precision, and Material Range
items.blurb: Direct Ink Additive Lithography spreads thick, paste-like inks into thin sheets then uses patterned light to selectively cure them — combining light-based precision with extrusion-compatible material range, including particle-filled inks that scatter light and have historically defeated photopolymer printers. Crucially, it eliminates support structures for overhanging features, which is the practical bottleneck for complex geometries. Published in Science Advances this week; the material compatibility angle opens fabrication territory that neither SLA nor FDM could reach.

items.title: Kelly Sinnapah Mary: Bodies as Ecology, Ancestry as Living Foliage
items.blurb: Mary's recurring figure Sanbras — reclaimed from a 19th-century colonial children's book — appears tattooed with verdant foliage, neither fully human nor fully plant, emerging from and subsumed by Caribbean flora. The work is autobiographically entangled: Mary grew up identifying as Afro-Caribbean, then discovered she descends from Tamil Nadu indentured workers brought to Guadeloupe after abolition, which bent her entire framework for understanding place, body, and belonging. The images hit like surrealism that earned its strangeness.

items.title: Son Lux — 'Out Into Us'
items.blurb: Joint commission from MASS MoCA and Pioneer Works — two institutions that treat music video as a serious medium — directed by Alex Cook for Son Lux, who have spent a decade making records about grief, temporality, and the gap between what's felt and what can be said. Pioneer Works commissions don't get made carelessly. Worth the runtime.

facts.fact: France's IRGC-attributed cyberattack targeted supermarket refrigeration systems nationwide — the first known case of a nation-state hacking cold-chain infrastructure at scale.

AlphaProof Code produced 6.5 million lines of Lean proof to verify Signal's cryptography at the compiled AArch64 binary level — the first formal verification of any widely deployed protocol's actual implementation, by any method.

Triangle Splatting renders the Garden scene at over 2,400 FPS at 1280×720 using a standard off-the-shelf mesh renderer — roughly the speed of a game engine, with photogrammetry-quality reconstruction.

Claude Code's 'Yes, and don't ask again' approval sometimes writes the full shell command — including embedded passwords and API keys — directly into a settings file that isn't blocked at the repo level, leading to over 100,000 exposed instances on public GitHub.

make_something.prompt: Triangle Splatting renders photogrammetry captures using native GPU triangle primitives, hitting 2,400 FPS on hardware you already own. Take a single object — something with a complicated edge or fine surface detail that Gaussian splats tend to blur — scan it with your phone, run it through the Triangle Splatting pipeline (code is released), and pipe the resulting mesh into a WebGL viewer. See where the triangle representation holds detail that 3DGS loses, and where it fails. The goal isn't a finished piece — it's calibrating your eye to what the primitive actually does.

art_picks.title: Leviathan
art_picks.creator: Lucien Castaing-Taylor & Véréna Paravel (Sensory Ethnography Lab)
art_picks.why: A fully non-narrative documentary shot entirely on small cameras attached to fishing nets, cables, and the bodies of fishermen — it dissolves the boundary between observer and system, turning industrial labor into something genuinely hallucinatory. The kind of film that rewires how you look at any physical process.

art_picks.title: Early Computer Art / Plotter Drawings (Frieder Nake, Vera Molnár, Georg Nees)
art_picks.creator: Various — curated entry point via the DAM Collection
art_picks.why: The founding generation of generative art, working in the 1960s when writing code to draw was genuinely absurd — Molnár's obsessive hand-plotted grids map straight onto Willem's interest in systems as self-expression, and the aesthetic is still more interesting than most contemporary generative work.

art_picks.title: Vespertine
art_picks.creator: Björk
art_picks.why: A album built entirely from micro-sounds — ice cracking, music boxes, beats made from shuffled cards — that behaves more like an ecosystem than a pop record. The production logic is inseparable from the emotional world it creates; it's a system that generates feeling.

events.name: Art Week NYC — Inaugural Edition
events.venue: Citywide (Chelsea, Tribeca, LES, UES + New Museum hub, 235 Bowery)
events.why: The first citywide contemporary art festival organized by Artforum, ARTnews, and the New Museum — 76+ galleries doing simultaneous openings across four neighborhoods, culminating in a full day of public talks at the New Museum on 'Art and the City' with artists, architects, filmmakers, and critics; not a fair, but a live scene made briefly legible.

events.name: Per Kirkeby: Shadows to the Feast
events.why: Opening during Art Week NYC — Kirkeby is the rare painter who thought seriously about geology and deep time, whose surfaces read as landscape and also as systems; worth catching at opening when the room is still readable.

events.name: Doris Salcedo — 'House' (Opening)
events.venue: White Cube New York, 1002 Madison Avenue
events.why: A nearly 30-foot full-scale house woven entirely from human hair, made over three years with 20 Colombian women who survived conflict — Salcedo's first major New York installation in over a decade, and the kind of object that makes you feel the weight of a political fact rather than just understand it.

events.name: Danny Brown
events.why: One of the most formally interesting rappers working — his records collapse genre and mood in ways that feel closer to sound design than hip-hop convention, and 1,000-cap Irving Plaza is the right size to feel that in the room.

events.name: MCNY: 'New York Now: After Dark' (Opening)
events.venue: Museum of the City of New York, 1220 Fifth Avenue
events.why: MCNY's triennial of contemporary photography, this edition focused entirely on the city after dark — the overlap of work, leisure, ambition, and escape in the nighttime landscape that makes New York's social systems most visible.
